title: Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, requiring a separate short scholarship application after a full course offer is received
implementing_agency: Macquarie University - Scholarships Team and International Student Office (scholarships@mq.edu.au / study@mq.edu.au)
programme_action: Macquarie University international scholarship programme - Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship (VCIS) band
description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship (VCIS) is a merit-based tuition-fee scholarship awarded by Macquarie University to full-time international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree. Undergraduate applicants must achieve a minimum ATAR equivalent of 85 and hold a full offer to study at Macquarie University. The award is a one-off fee reduction of up to AUD $10,000 applied towards tuition fees; the University describes it as highly competitive and very limited. It is not automatic on admission - the applicant must first receive a full course offer and then complete a short online scholarship application form.

award_types: One-off tuition fee reduction (up to AUD $10,000)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: The official key-details panel lists Award value '(Fee reduction) Up to AUD $10,000' and Duration 'One-off award'. The stated purpose is to reward academic excellence and attract high performing students to study at Macquarie University.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Not renewable. The official page records the Duration as 'One-off award' and publishes no renewal, continuing-eligibility or re-application criteria for VCIS.
programme_structure.intake: Open year round. The recipient must commence study in the session and year stated in the scholarship letter of offer; Macquarie's Session 1 2027 runs 22 February - 25 June 2027 with orientation 15-19 February 2027.

status_note: The official VCIS page publishes 'Applications close: Open year round', so there is no fixed calendar closing date. Applications for 2027 entry are open and are assessed on a rolling basis. Because Macquarie describes the award as very limited and states that applications run 'open year round or until scholarships have been filled up for the year', the effective window can close before a given intake once the available pool is exhausted. Recipients must accept by the date stated in their offer letter. Next expected cycle after 2027 entry is 2028 entry on the same year-round basis; re-check the official page before each intake.
verification_type: Official university award page, official English-language and academic entry requirement pages, and the official Macquarie online scholarship application form
verification_notes: Verified directly on mq.edu.au. Confirmed: award name, 'up to AUD $10,000' value, fee-reduction instrument, 'One-off award' duration, 'Open year round' closing, undergraduate ATAR-equivalent threshold of 85, full-offer prerequisite, the separate short online scholarship application, applicable course 'All', and the two-stage assessment/outcome timetable. English thresholds and accepted tests were taken from the official English language requirements page, using the 'Required Scores - From 1 March 2026' table that governs 2027 entry. Admission-route and offer-acceptance requirements were taken from the official international applications and international offers pages. The official Macquarie University logo asset was loaded and rendered as a real 158x48 PNG on the mq.edu.au domain. Items that could not be confirmed are listed in verification.unverified_or_removed_claims.
source_last_updated: 2026-07-15 (last-updated stamp published on Macquarie's linked international academic entry requirements page). The VCIS award page itself and the English language requirements page publish no last-updated date.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Open year round (rolling). Macquarie advises accepting the offer and scholarship early because the award is very limited and can be exhausted.
application_deadline.application_period: Rolling year-round across all intakes. The scholarship application may only be lodged after a full course offer has been received, and the recipient must commence in the session and year stated in the scholarship letter of offer.
application_deadline.official_rule: The official VCIS page lists 'Applications close: Open year round' and states 'This is a very limited scholarship, so we encourage you to accept your offer and scholarship early to avoid disappointment.' The international scholarships overview page states that applications are 'Generally... open year round or until scholarships have been filled up for the year' and that 'You will be required to accept your scholarship by the date indiciated in your Offer Letter.' No calendar closing date, cut-off time or timezone is published for VCIS, so deadline_date is null and deadline_precision is 'typical_window' rather than 'exact'. Session 1 2027 itself runs 22 February - 25 June 2027.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The absence of a published cut-off does not mean unlimited capacity. Macquarie states the scholarship is 'very limited' and that awards are made until scholarships have been filled for the year; the 2027 International Student Guide states that the annual number of recipients varies with available funding and eligible candidates and is only confirmed when an offer letter is made. Submit the scholarship form as soon as the full course offer arrives.

programme_duration.renewal_note: The official key-details panel lists Duration as 'One-off award'. No renewal, continuation or re-application-while-enrolled criteria are published for VCIS. The funded bachelor degree itself typically runs 3-4 years depending on the course.

funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend, living allowance or cost-of-living payment is published for VCIS. The award is a tuition fee reduction only.
funding.travel_amount_note: The official VCIS page publishes no travel, airfare or relocation allowance.
funding.institutional_costs: Tuition fees only. International student course fees are set per credit point and revised each year. The scholarship contributes no part of the compulsory Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), the Student Services and Amenities Fee (SSAF), textbooks, accommodation or living costs.
funding.fully_funded_note: VCIS is a partial, one-off tuition fee reduction of up to AUD $10,000. It does not cover living costs, travel, insurance or the Student Services and Amenities Fee, and it is not a full scholarship. It must not be described as fully funded.

tuition.conditions: One-off fee reduction applied towards tuition fees for a commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree. The exact amount is 'up to' the stated maximum, is at the University's discretion, and is only confirmed in the scholarship letter of offer.

insurance.note: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is compulsory for student visa holders and is paid by the student; VCIS does not cover it.

bond.note: No service bond or return-home requirement is published for VCIS on the official award page. An archived students.mq.edu.au VCIS page did state that a student who withdraws before completion may be required to repay scholarship already awarded, as decided by the scholarships and grants committee; that language does not appear on the current official award page.

total_estimated_value.note: The award is expressed as 'up to AUD $10,000'. The official source does not publish a fixed value or a total package value, so no total has been computed.

coverage: Tuition fee reduction of up to AUD $10,000 (one-off), credited against tuition fees
coverage_limitations: The amount is 'up to' AUD $10,000; the actual value awarded is not guaranteed and is only stated in the scholarship letter of offer.
One-off payment only - there is no renewal for later years of the degree.
No living allowance, travel allowance, installation allowance, insurance or accommodation support is published.
Living costs, compulsory Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), textbooks and the Student Services and Amenities Fee (SSAF) remain the student's responsibility.
The number of awards is very limited; the University states the annual number of recipients may vary with available funding and eligible candidates and is only confirmed at offer.
Exclusions and benefit structure may change between intakes; the values and rules published for 2027 entry may not apply in later cycles.
eligible_applicants: Full-time international students (not Australian or New Zealand citizens, not Australian permanent residents, not holders of a permanent Australian humanitarian visa) commencing an undergraduate coursework degree
Students who hold a full offer to study at Macquarie University and meet the course's academic and English entry requirements
Applicants achieving a minimum ATAR equivalent of 85 for undergraduate applications
Students able to commence study in the session and year indicated in the scholarship letter of offer
Other study levels (e.g. Macquarie University College pathway programs, Study Abroad) may be considered on a case-by-case basis
final_year_condition: VCIS is awarded to students commencing a bachelor's degree, so the relevant 'final year' is the final year of secondary school (or the final year of an equivalent pre-tertiary qualification). Because the scholarship form can only be lodged after a full course offer, a student still completing final-year examinations must wait until Macquarie issues a full (not conditional) offer before applying.
equivalent_degree_note: Yes. Macquarie assesses entry to undergraduate degrees from a recognised senior secondary school qualification or university entrance examination (e.g. NSW HSC or overseas equivalent), a recognised university Foundation course, a recognised 2-3 year Diploma / Advanced Diploma / Associate Degree, or at least one year of a recognised bachelor degree. Overseas qualifications are converted to an international selection rank / ATAR equivalent; the VCIS undergraduate threshold is expressed as an ATAR equivalent of 85.

age_limit.official_source: No age limit is published for VCIS on the official award page. Separately, Macquarie requires international applicants who will be under 18 at course commencement to have approved welfare arrangements in place for visa purposes (International Under 18 Welfare Arrangement form, Form 157N nomination of a student guardian, or a University-approved homestay provider).

eligibility.citizenship: Open to international students of all nationalities. Macquarie defines an international student as someone who is not an Australian or New Zealand citizen, does not hold Australian permanent resident status and does not hold a permanent Australian humanitarian visa. VCIS has no eligible-country list (unlike Macquarie's country or regional scholarships such as the $15,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship for Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam).
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement is published. The applicant must be a full-time international student commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Macquarie University.
eligibility.age_limit: No age limit published. Applicants under 18 at commencement must satisfy University and Department of Home Affairs welfare-arrangement requirements.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Undergraduate applicants must achieve a minimum ATAR equivalent of 85 and must hold a full offer for the course. The academic entry requirements of the specific course (international selection rank / cut-off) still apply.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Not expressed as a GPA. The published undergraduate threshold is an ATAR equivalent of 85. The 'minimum WAM equivalent of 65' criterion applies only to postgraduate applicants and does not apply to bachelor's applicants.
eligibility.language_requirement: Applicants must meet the English language requirements of the course they have been offered (for most undergraduate courses, Competent English = IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each section).
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: None required and none published. The official page describes selection as based on academic merit.
eligibility.financial_need: Not a criterion. VCIS is explicitly merit-based and no means test is published.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Students can generally receive only one Macquarie scholarship at a time, with exceptions possible; contact study@mq.edu.au if more than one is offered.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Full-time international student commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, commencing in the session and year indicated in the scholarship letter of offer.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health requirement for the scholarship. Compulsory Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is required for a student visa and is a separate cost.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None for VCIS - the official page lists 'Applicable course: All'. Course exclusions published for some other Macquarie international scholarships do not apply here.
eligibility.previous_award_restriction: Macquarie states that students can generally receive only one scholarship at a time, although exceptions are possible; applicants offered more than one scholarship are advised to contact study@mq.edu.au. No restriction specific to a previous Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarship applies, as VCIS is a bachelor's-level award.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: The published undergraduate threshold is an ATAR equivalent of 85, not a fixed percentage or grade-point average.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Course-specific academic entry requirements still apply. International applicants must hold a recognised senior secondary qualification or accepted alternative, and must meet the international selection rank / cut-off score for the specific degree. Some degrees set higher thresholds than the general minimum.
selection_factors_may_include: Academic merit, evidenced by a minimum ATAR equivalent of 85 for undergraduate applicants
Meeting the academic and English entry requirements of the offered Macquarie course
Timeliness of the application and offer acceptance, because the number of awards is very limited
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: The official page describes VCIS as 'a highly competitive scholarship based on academic merit'. No portfolio, interview, audition, community-service or leadership criterion is published for VCIS.

english_requirement.minimum_ielts: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each of Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking (Competent English, the standard required for most undergraduate courses). Higher bands apply to some degrees: Proficient English 7.0 overall (6.5 in each section) for Bachelor of Clinical Science, Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science and Bachelor of Laws; Advanced English 7.5 overall (7.0 Reading, 7.0 Writing, 8.0 Listening, 8.0 Speaking) for the Bachelor of Education degrees.
english_requirement.minimum_toefl: TOEFL iBT, old scoring table: 86 overall (Reading 18, Writing 20, Listening 17, Speaking 20) for Competent English. TOEFL iBT, new scoring scale: 4.5 overall (4 in each section) for Competent English.
english_requirement.minimum_pte: PTE Academic 60 overall with Reading 51, Writing 55, Listening 50 and Speaking 54 (Competent English, per the 'Required Scores - From 1 March 2026' table that governs 2027 entry).
english_requirement.moi_rule: Macquarie accepts a recognised qualification with English as the language of instruction as one form of evidence of English proficiency, alongside an approved test, an approved Foundation program, a Macquarie University College English Language Program, or another approved English for Academic Purposes program.
english_requirement.test_score_note: English thresholds are set by the course, not by the scholarship, and must not be universalised. Most undergraduate courses require 'Competent English'; some require Proficient (IELTS 7.0 overall) or Advanced (IELTS 7.5 overall) English; Macquarie University College Foundation and Diploma programs require IELTS 5.5 and 6.0 respectively. VCIS applicants must meet the English requirement of the course they have been offered. The figures above are from the 'Required Scores - From 1 March 2026' table on the official English language requirements page, which applies to 2027 entry.
accepted_tests: TOEFL iBT (old scoring table and new scoring scale; test-date rules apply for visa purposes)
LanguageCert Academic (test-centre sittings only; the online version is not accepted)
Cambridge English C1 Advanced (C1A, previously CAE)
Cambridge English C2 Proficiency (C2P, previously CPE)

Duolingo English Test (DET) - accepted only for applicants of Standard Foundation, Study Abroad and Exchange, and remote students where attending a test centre would result in hardship, and for approved Transnational Education (TNE) programs case by case

language_of_instruction.language_note: Macquarie University coursework degrees are taught in English. Macquarie University College English Language Programs and approved English for Academic Purposes programs are available for applicants who need to reach the required standard before commencing a degree.

application_method.application_route: Two-stage. Stage 1 - apply for admission: via the Universities Admissions Centre (UAC) for applicants completing an Australian Year 12 qualification (NSW HSC or interstate equivalent, in or outside Australia), an IB Diploma in Australia, or NZ NCEA Level 3; all other international applicants apply directly to Macquarie University online or through an authorised agent. Stage 2 - after receiving a full offer, submit the single online International Scholarship Application Form and select 'Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship'.
application_steps: Prepare and lodge a course application for the undergraduate degree you intend to study, directly to Macquarie University online, through an authorised agent, or via UAC if you are completing an Australian Year 12, IB or NCEA qualification.
Meet the academic and English entry requirements for the course applied for, holding a recognised senior secondary qualification or accepted equivalent.

Wait for a full (unconditional) Letter of Offer. The scholarship form can only be submitted after a full offer has been received, and the offer contains the Macquarie University Student ID required on the form.
Complete the online International Scholarship Application Form, entering title, first name, last name, Macquarie University Student ID, email address and date of birth.
Select 'Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship' as the scholarship being applied for, and select your country of citizenship and study level (Bachelor program for undergraduate applicants).
Read and type your name to confirm the declaration that the information provided is true and accurate, and submit the form. Only ONE submission is required.

Receive the outcome by email: applications submitted on a Monday generally receive an outcome by Friday of the same week; applications submitted after Monday receive an outcome by Friday of the following week.

If successful, accept the offer and the scholarship by the date stated in the Letter of Offer, and pay any applicable commencement fee (recipients of tuition scholarships may be exempt, as specified in the letter of offer).
Enrol in the course and commence in the session and year stated in the scholarship letter of offer.

Overseas qualifications are converted to an international selection rank.
official_application_documents.document_language: Supporting documents must be in English or accompanied by an English translation.
official_application_documents.document_format: Online submission only. The scholarship application is a web form; no paper or emailed application is offered.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Academic qualification results are assessed as part of the admission application, which must be completed and result in a full offer before the scholarship form can be lodged.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: Documents not issued in English must be accompanied by a translation. The VCIS page does not state whether certification by a translator is required; applicants should confirm with their Admissions Officer.

identity_documents.status: Required on the scholarship application form

academic_documents.status: Required for admission; assessed before the scholarship application

selection_process.decision_maker: Macquarie University Scholarships Team, with assessment by a scholarship selection committee
possible_stages: Lodge the course application and satisfy the course's academic and English entry requirements
Receive a full (unconditional) Letter of Offer from Macquarie University
Submit the online International Scholarship Application Form selecting the Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship
Assessment by the Scholarships Team against the published criteria (ATAR equivalent of 85 for undergraduate applicants)
Outcome notified by email, and the scholarship articulated in the scholarship letter of offer
Accept the offer and scholarship by the date stated in the letter of offer and commence in the stated session and year
selection_process.weighting_note: No numerical weighting or scoring rubric is published. Macquarie describes VCIS as 'a highly competitive scholarship based on academic merit'.
selection_process.results_timing: Applications submitted on a Monday generally receive an outcome by Friday of the same week; applications submitted after Monday receive an outcome by Friday of the following week. The outcome is notified via email.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: No ranking, banding or class-of-award system is published. Awards are drawn from a limited pool, and the University says the annual number of recipients varies with available funding and eligible candidates.

additional_factors: Holding a full offer for the relevant course and intake
Commencing study in the session and year indicated in the scholarship letter of offer
Applying early, because the scholarship is very limited and awarded until the pool is exhausted

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree at Macquarie University (single or double degree). The scholarship funds the degree; it is not itself a qualification.
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 3-4 years for most Macquarie bachelor degrees; course-specific, see Coursefinder.
possible_awards: Bachelor's degree with Honours where offered by the course
degree_outcome.degree_note: Macquarie University bachelor degrees are regulated under the Australian Qualifications Framework and delivered within the Education Services for Overseas Students (ESOS) framework. Undergraduate units are 1000-5000 level.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Recognition of prior learning (RPL) may be available and can reduce programme length. RPL is assessed separately from the scholarship and does not affect VCIS eligibility.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: A tuition fee reduction of up to AUD $10,000 (one-off) applied towards tuition fees. Recipients remain liable for the balance of tuition fees, which are set on a per credit point basis and revised each year; fees are payable at the beginning of each session (January and July).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application fee is published for the VCIS scholarship form. The international commencement fee is usually AU$16,000-AU$23,500 depending on course and is offset against first-session tuition, not charged in addition to it. Macquarie states that recipients of tuition scholarships may be exempt from paying a commencement fee, with details specified in the letter of offer.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Once admitted, students are bound by Macquarie's enrolment Terms and Conditions (eStudent) and the Student Charter / Student Code of Conduct. A Scholarship Acceptance form is submitted when accepting an offer where applicable.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients receive the same access as other Macquarie students to standard student services and support. Macquarie operates within the ESOS framework, and recipients of the scholarship are subject to the same tuition, refund and progression policies as other international students. Scholarship application is applied and can be checked in eStudent under 'View student finances'.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No service bond or return-home requirement is published for VCIS. An archived students.mq.edu.au VCIS page stated that a student who withdraws before completion may be required to repay scholarship already awarded, as decided by the scholarships and grants committee; that repayment language does not appear on the current official award page and should be confirmed with the Scholarships Team.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you meet Macquarie's definition of an international student (not an Australian or New Zealand citizen, not an Australian permanent resident, no permanent Australian humanitarian visa)
Select your undergraduate degree and check its international selection rank / cut-off and English requirement on Coursefinder
Confirm your qualification converts to an ATAR equivalent of at least 85
Book and sit an approved English test with results less than two years old at course commencement
Lodge the course application early (direct, agent or UAC) and respond quickly to admissions requests
Track your application until a full (not conditional) Letter of Offer arrives and note your Macquarie University Student ID
Complete the online International Scholarship Application Form immediately after receiving the full offer
Accept the offer and scholarship by the stated deadline and pay any applicable commencement fee
Apply for your student visa using the Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) and arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC)
programme_comparison_fields: Award value (one-off AUD $10,000 maximum vs AUD $15,000 per year for Macquarie's country/regional and partner-institution scholarships)
Nationality restriction (none for VCIS vs country lists for other Macquarie international scholarships)
Application requirement (separate form for VCIS vs automatic assessment for some other Macquarie international scholarships)
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No motivation letter, personal statement or scholarship essay is required. The International Scholarship Application Form asks only for identity details, the Macquarie University Student ID, the scholarship selected, country of citizenship and study level, plus a typed-name declaration. Effort is better spent on securing and accepting the full course offer quickly and on making sure the academic and English results already lodged are accurate and complete, since assessment is merit-based on the ATAR equivalent.
profile_fit_labels: High-achieving international secondary school leaver (ATAR equivalent 85+)
Student who already holds or is about to receive a full Macquarie course offer
Applicant seeking a modest one-off tuition contribution rather than a full ride
Applicant from any country (no nationality list applies)
Applicant who can commence in a specific session and year as stated in the offer
common_mistakes: Applying for the scholarship before receiving a full course offer - the form cannot be usefully submitted until then, because it requires the Macquarie University Student ID
Waiting until a later intake on the assumption that 'open year round' means capacity is guaranteed - the award is described as very limited and can be exhausted
Assuming the award is renewable across the years of the degree - it is explicitly a one-off award
Assuming the award covers living costs, travel, OSHC or the Student Services and Amenities Fee - it is a tuition fee reduction only
Using an English test result older than two years at course commencement
Assuming VCIS is automatic on admission - some other Macquarie international scholarships are automatic, but VCIS requires a separate application
Expecting to defer the scholarship - Macquarie states most scholarship offers cannot be deferred and the recipient must commence in the stated session and year

risk_flags.risk: The scholarship is described as 'very limited' and applications are open until scholarships have been filled for the year, so the pool can be exhausted without notice.
risk_flags.impact: An otherwise eligible applicant may receive no award despite submitting on time.
risk_flags.mitigation: Submit the scholarship form immediately after the full offer arrives, accept the offer early, and apply for the earliest available session.

risk_flags.risk: The award value is 'up to' AUD $10,000 and the actual amount is at the University's discretion.
risk_flags.impact: Budget planning based on the full AUD $10,000 may overestimate the benefit.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as a partial offset only; confirm the actual amount in the scholarship letter of offer before committing financially.

risk_flags.risk: VCIS is a one-off award and does not renew for later years of the degree.
risk_flags.impact: Years 2-4 of the degree carry full tuition liability.
risk_flags.mitigation: Model total degree cost assuming the award is received once, and check whether another Macquarie scholarship (for example a country or regional scholarship paid for the full course duration) is available in later rounds.

risk_flags.risk: The recipient must commence in the session and year stated in the offer letter, and Macquarie states most scholarship offers cannot be deferred.
risk_flags.impact: A visa delay, deferred commencement or change of plan can forfeit the award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply for the visa immediately after the Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) is issued, and note that after acceptance a deferral is only possible on compassionate or compelling grounds.

risk_flags.risk: English and academic entry thresholds are course-specific and change (a new score table applies from 1 March 2026).
risk_flags.impact: Meeting the general minimum does not guarantee meeting the requirement of a higher-threshold degree such as Laws or Education.
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the specific course's requirement on Coursefinder and the current English language requirements page before sitting a test.

risk_flags.risk: Changing enrolment (transferring course, reducing study load, suspending studies) may affect continuing eligibility.
risk_flags.impact: A later scholarship revocation or repayment claim.
risk_flags.mitigation: Macquarie instructs students to notify the Scholarships Team at scholarships@mq.edu.au before making any change to enrolment.

risk_flags.risk: The award page publishes no last-updated date, so the value, thresholds or exclusions could change between intakes.
risk_flags.impact: Details recorded for 2027 entry may not apply in later cycles.
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-read the official VCIS page and the international scholarships overview page before each application round; next scheduled verification 2027-04-03.

risk_flags.risk: Macquarie students can generally hold only one scholarship at a time.
risk_flags.impact: A VCIS award may preclude stacking another Macquarie scholarship, or the University may award only one of several.
risk_flags.mitigation: If offered more than one scholarship, contact study@mq.edu.au before accepting, as exceptions are possible.

Scholarship assessment by the Macquarie Scholarships Team

Scholarship offered in the scholarship letter of offer

best_fit: A high-achieving international secondary school leaver (ATAR equivalent 85 or above) from any country who wants to study a bachelor's degree at Macquarie University in Sydney, who is comfortable self-funding the bulk of tuition and living costs and is looking for a modest one-off tuition offset. Particularly suited to applicants who can move quickly: they are organised enough to lodge the admission application early, respond fast to offer conditions, and submit the short scholarship form as soon as the full offer arrives.
not_best_fit: Applicants who cannot achieve an ATAR equivalent of at least 85
Applicants seeking a full scholarship, a living allowance, travel money or accommodation support
Applicants who need funding in every year of the degree, since VCIS is a one-off award
Citizens of Australia or New Zealand and Australian permanent residents, who are not international students at Macquarie
Applicants who cannot commence in the specific session and year stated in the offer letter, or who need to defer
Applicants who want a scholarship awarded automatically on admission without a separate application (VCIS requires a separate form)

database_notes: Target assignment: Macquarie University international undergraduate scholarships. The current, broadly open, country-neutral international undergraduate scholarship on mq.edu.au is the Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship (VCIS), so that is the award recorded here.

The task also named a 'Macquarie University International Scholarship'. No award with that exact name is published on mq.edu.au today; the only official award matching the description and open to all nationalities is the Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship. 'Macquarie University Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship' is recorded as a legacy title because it is used in the official summary text on the students.mq.edu.au staging page for this award. No other legacy title has been invented.

Macquarie's other international scholarships are either country or region locked (for example the Macquarie University $15,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship for citizens of Indonesia, the Philippines and Vietnam; the Lebanon $10,000 Early Acceptance Scholarship), pathway specific (Macquarie University College $5,000 and $3,000 Scholarships), partner-institution specific (Partner Institution Scholarship and ASEAN Partner Institution Scholarship), or faculty/demographic specific (Faculty of Science and Engineering Women in STEM Scholarship, AUD $5,000, applications for 2027 not yet open). Per the research protocol these region- or nationality-locked awards were not substituted, because the protocol prefers broadly-open awards.

VCIS covers both bachelor's and master's coursework degrees. This record is filed as a bachelor's record per the assigned target; the postgraduate WAM-equivalent-65 criterion is recorded only to mark it as not applicable to undergraduate applicants.
The award is a partial tuition fee reduction only and must not be presented as fully funded. No total value has been computed from the 'up to AUD $10,000' figure.

Deadline honesty: the official page publishes 'Applications close: Open year round' with no calendar date or timezone, so deadline_date is null and deadline_precision is 'typical_window'. The only date-like information published relates to the funded degree's session dates (Session 1 2027: 22 February - 25 June 2027) and to the offer-acceptance deadline stated in each individual offer letter.

Verification timestamps follow the reference date given in SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md (2026-10-03) rather than the wall-clock time of the browsing session; all content was read live from the official pages during this session.

Verification confidence is 0.93 rather than higher because the number of awards, the exact awarded amount within the 'up to' range, any course exclusions, and a possible withdrawal-repayment obligation could not be confirmed from the current official award page.

Direct HTTP requests to mq.edu.au assets return a Cloudflare 403 challenge; all page content was therefore read through the fetch tool and a headless browser session, which is sufficient for verification but means no byte-level caching check was performed.

Logo: a real official Macquarie University logo asset on the mq.edu.au domain was found, loaded and measured (158x48 PNG), so logo_url is populated rather than null. No third-party, aggregator, Wikipedia or stock logo was used.

The archived students.mq.edu.au VCIS page lists older conditions (commencing in 2021 or 2022, 8 standard units per academic year full-time load, exclusion of Macquarie University International College applicants, exclusion of other Macquarie scholarship recipients, and possible repayment on withdrawal). Those are historical and are not treated as current criteria; only the live mq.edu.au award page was used for the eligibility fields.
